description: Table 3 is a single rendered data table (no plots, micrographs or scale bars) headed "Samples" / "Rolling states" and captioned "Tensile experiment of rolling (1050 °C) Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–xBe steels." It is organised in four rows — 0Be, 0.5Be, 1.0Be, 1.5Be — under five data columns: ρ (g/cm³) with an "Error" column, then the three rolling-state tensile quantities YS (MPa), UST (MPa) and TE (%). Every cell is legible and no cell is blank. Density falls monotonically with Be addition: 6.54 ±0.03, 6.47 ±0.02, 6.36 ±0.04 and 6.29 ±0.05 g/cm³, the error bracket growing with Be content. Yield strength is non-monotonic: 989.51 → 1011.54 → 820.57 → 941.87 MPa, i.e. a small rise at 0.5Be, a minimum at 1.0Be, then a recovery at 1.5Be. UST behaves roughly oppositely: 1222.27 → 1130.18 → 1074.33 → 1201.58 MPa, falling to a minimum at 1.0Be before rising again, but the 1.5Be value stays below the 0Be value. Total elongation peaks sharply at 0.5Be (40.47 %), with 22.91 %, 30.71 % and 18.33 % for 0Be, 1.0Be and 1.5Be respectively. The table thus provides the quantitative tensile and density backing for the stress–strain and work-hardening curves referred to as Figure 10(a, b).

observations.observation: Table 3 is a text table, not a plot: header groups are "Samples" and "Rolling states", with data columns ρ (g/cm³), Error, YS (MPa), UST (MPa) and TE (%).
Density decreases monotonically with Be content: 6.54, 6.47, 6.36 and 6.29 g/cm³ for 0Be, 0.5Be, 1.0Be and 1.5Be respectively.
Density error increases with Be content: ±0.03, ±0.02, ±0.04 and ±0.05 g/cm³ for 0Be, 0.5Be, 1.0Be and 1.5Be.
Yield strength (YS) is non-monotonic: 989.51 MPa (0Be), 1011.54 MPa (0.5Be), 820.57 MPa (1.0Be) and 941.87 MPa (1.5Be), with the minimum at 1.0Be.
UST is 1222.27 MPa (0Be), 1130.18 MPa (0.5Be), 1074.33 MPa (1.0Be) and 1201.58 MPa (1.5Be), i.e. a minimum at 1.0Be with a subsequent rise that still stays below the 0Be value.
Total elongation peaks at 0.5Be (40.47 %) and is otherwise 22.91 % (0Be), 30.71 % (1.0Be) and 18.33 % (1.5Be), so 0.5Be is both the highest-strength-YZ and most ductile condition in the table.
The 0Be sample has the highest UST (1222.27 MPa) but the second-lowest TE (22.91 %), while 0.5Be trades a small UST drop for the largest elongation.
The caption states the table reports the tensile experiment on rolled (1050 °C) Fe–30Mn–10Al–1.5C–xBe steels.

The citing text states that with increasing Be content the yield strength initially increases, then decreases and finally increases, while tensile strength shows the opposite trend (initially decreases, finally increases); the table values agree for YS but UST at 1.5Be (1201.58 MPa) remains below the 0Be value (1222.27 MPa).
The citing text states that Table 3 gives the detailed tensile-property values corresponding to the engineering stress–strain and work-hardening curves of Figure 10(a, b).
